solutions.latex: $$\int_0^k\sin x\,dx=1$$ $$\left[-\cos x\right]_0^k=1$$ $$-[\cos k-\cos 0]=1$$ $$-[\cos k-1]=1$$ $$\cos k-1=-1$$ $$\cos k=0$$ $$k=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$$ Answer: A

Area of trapezium above the axis $=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 10(2+5)=35$.

Area of trapezium below the axis: $35=\dfrac{1}{2}(k-4)(4+6)$, so $35=5(k-4)$, $7=k-4$, $k=11$. Answer: C

Ordered data: 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 17, 19, 28. $Q_1=12.5$, $Q_2=16$, $Q_3=18$.

Lower quartile is $12.5$; upper quartile is $18$.

$$(\tan x)^2=3,\quad \tan x=\pm\sqrt3$$ Related angle $=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ (all four quadrants):

$$x=\dfrac{\pi}{3},\dfrac{2\pi}{3},\dfrac{4\pi}{3},\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$$

Venn diagram: only The Office 5, both 7, only Stranger Things 6, neither 5.

$$P(\text{neither})=\dfrac{5}{23}$$

Stationary points occur when $f'(x)=0$. $f'(x)=3x^2-6x-9$, so $3x^2-6x-9=0$, $3(x^2-2x-3)=0$, $3(x-3)(x+1)=0$, giving $x=3$ or $x=-1$.

When $x=3$, $y=-21$; when $x=-1$, $y=11$.

$f''(x)=6x-6$. At $x=3$: $f''(3)=12>0$, so a minimum turning point at $(3,-21)$. At $x=-1$: $f''(-1)=-12<0$, so a maximum turning point at $(-1,11)$.

Points of inflexion occur when $f''(x)=0$: $6x-6=0$, $x=1$. When $x=1$, $y=-5$. Possible point of inflexion at $(1,-5)$.

Concavity check: $f''(0)=-6$, $f''(1)=0$, $f''(2)=6$. As concavity changes, $(1,-5)$ is a point of inflexion.
Sketch $y=1-x$ (y-intercept 1, x-intercept 1). There are 3 points of intersection, so 3 solutions.
Circumference of cone base $=2\pi\theta$ and $C=2\pi r$, so $2\pi r=2\pi\theta$ and $r=\theta$.

$V=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\left(4\theta^4-\theta^6\right)^{\frac12}$. Maximum when $V'=0$:

$$V'=\dfrac{\pi}{6}\left(4\theta^4-\theta^6\right)^{-\frac12}\left(16\theta^3-6\theta^5\right)=\dfrac{\pi(16\theta^3-6\theta^5)}{6\sqrt{4\theta^4-\theta^6}}$$ $16\theta^3-6\theta^5=0$, $2\theta^3(8-3\theta^2)=0$, $\theta\ne0$ so $\theta^2=\dfrac83$, $\theta=\sqrt{\dfrac83}=1.63$ (2 d.p.).

Nature: $V'(1)=3.02>0$, $V'(1.63)=0$, $V'(1.8)=-3.72<0$, so a maximum when $\theta=1.63$.
